source.section: PDF page 9, Line 29 ($20,000 limit regardless of the source; periodic payments; IRA payments); Form IT-201 line 15 and line 27 (Social Security); Form IT-201 line 29; Form IT-201 lines 19, 24, 32-39 (PDF pages 2-3); IT-201-I PDF page 11 (line 34 standard deduction table), PDF pages 12 and 33 (line 39, rate schedule)

worked: Single, 67: Pennsylvania state (PSERS) pension 85,000, IRA distribution 10,000, Social Security 30,000 gross. Federal taxable Social Security: provisional income 85,000 + 10,000 + 15,000 = 110,000; 85% x 30,000 = 25,500 is the lesser figure, so 25,500 taxable. Federal AGI = 85,000 + 10,000 + 25,500 = 120,500. Federal AGI (IT-201 line 19) = 120,500.00. Federal taxable income = 120,500.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction - 1 x 2,000 age-65 addition = 102,750.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Subtraction: line 27 taxable Social Security (exempt in full) 25,500.00. Subtraction: line 29 pension and annuity income exclusion: Pennsylvania state pension 85,000 + IRA 10,000 = 95,000, limited to 20,000 20,000.00. Line 32 total subtractions = 45,500.00. Line 33 New York AGI = 120,500.00 - 45,500.00 = 75,000.00. Line 34 New York standard deduction (single, PDF page 11 table) 8,000.00; line 35 = 75,000.00 - 8,000.00 = 67,000.00; line 36 dependent exemption 0 (no dependents); lines 37/38 taxable income 67,000.00. Rate schedule (PDF page 33, single) on 67,000.00: 8,500.00 x 4% = 340.00; 3,200.00 x 4.5% = 144.00; 2,200.00 x 5.25% = 115.50; 53,100.00 x 5.5% = 2,920.50; schedule tax = 3,520.00 (the printed schedule, with its whole-dollar base 600 at 13,900, gives 3,520.50; this case uses the bands as numbers). NY AGI is 107,650 or less and line 38 is 65,000 or more: the rate schedule applies (PDF page 12, line 39); no recapture worksheet. Line 39 NYS tax = 3,520.00. Credits: none (the household credit, line 40, PDF page 12 tables 1-3, allows no credit above federal AGI of 28,000 single or 32,000 other statuses): state income tax = 3,520.00.
